# Minecraft Server Manager (mcctl)

> mcctl puts every Minecraft Java Edition server you host behind a single port (25565). A server starts when the first player connects and stops after it goes idle, so an empty host runs only the router (about 40 MB of RAM). Servers run in Docker using itzg/minecraft-server, with itzg/mc-router for hostname routing. Manage everything from the CLI or a web console. Open source, Apache-2.0.

- Install: `npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl`, then `mcctl init`, `mcctl create`, `mcctl status`
- Requirements: Node.js 18+, Docker Engine 24+, Docker Compose 2.20+; Linux or macOS (Windows via WSL2)
- Connect by hostname: nip.io (`<server>.<host-ip>.nip.io:25565`), mDNS (`<server>.local`), or playit.gg for external access without port forwarding
- Server types: Paper, Vanilla, Forge, NeoForge, Fabric; mods and modpacks from Modrinth, CurseForge, Spiget
- Management Console: web UI (port 5000) and REST API (port 5001), set up with `mcctl console init`
- Backups: world backup to private GitHub repositories, cron-based scheduling

## FAQ

### What is Minecraft Server Manager (mcctl)?

A free, open-source (Apache-2.0) CLI and web console for running Minecraft Java Edition servers in Docker. Each server runs in its own `itzg/minecraft-server` container, and `itzg/mc-router` puts them all behind port 25565.

### How do I run multiple Minecraft servers on one port?

mc-router listens on port 25565 and sends each player to a server based on the hostname they connect to, such as `survival.192.168.1.100.nip.io` or `survival.local`. Every server is its own container, so you don't open a port per server. Connecting with a bare IP doesn't work, because the router needs a hostname.

### Do idle servers keep using RAM?

No. A server starts when the first player connects and stops after 10 minutes with no players (change it with `AUTO_SCALE_DOWN_AFTER`). When every server is stopped, only the router runs, using about 40 MB of RAM.

### Which server types and mods are supported?

Paper (the default), Vanilla, Forge, NeoForge, Fabric, Spigot, Bukkit, Purpur, and Quilt, plus Modrinth modpacks. You can search for mods and plugins and add them from Modrinth, CurseForge, and Spiget.

### Does it support Bedrock Edition?

No. It supports Minecraft Java Edition only.

### Can friends outside my home network join without port forwarding?

Yes. playit.gg tunneling gives your servers a public address without opening ports on your router. A VPN mesh such as Tailscale or ZeroTier also works.

### Is there a web interface?

Yes. `mcctl console init` sets up the Management Console: a web UI on port 5000 and a REST API on port 5001. From a browser you can manage servers, worlds, players, and server files.

### What do I need to run it?

Linux or macOS (Windows through WSL2) with Node.js 18+, Docker Engine 24+, and Docker Compose 2.20+. Install it with `npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl`. Players only need their usual Minecraft Java client.

### How are worlds backed up?

mcctl can push worlds to a private GitHub repository, and backups can run on a cron schedule with retention policies. You only need a GitHub account for the GitHub backup feature.
